messages:
incident-bot: INCIDENT P1 alert for tenant 'Vela Corp' — high 5xx rate in eu-west-2 dedicated pool. Trigger: healthcheck failures >5% over 3m. Paging on-call. Severity: CUSTOMER_IMPACT

maya-ops: seeing ~12% 5xx on the qps routing shard to vela-eu-west. Grafana shows latency spike + connection resets.

kevin-sre: confirmed. Errors originate from dedicated pool cluster vela-eu-west-pool-2. Instances reporting OOM logs then restart; kernel messages repeated.

sachin-eng: is this the pool that's on the private VPC link? Any recent deploys?

maya-ops: yes, it's the private VPC path. No code deploys in the last 2h per deploy-bot.

anna-support: Vela CS pinged asking if we have mitigation plan; customer is seeing degraded inference calls (timeouts ~10s then 5xx). They want ETA.

kevin-sre: short term plan: shift traffic from vela-eu-west-pool-2 -> vela-eu-west-warm-1 (warm capacity). We'll do a gradual weight shift (10% steps) and monitor errors. If errors drop, continue. Need DNS TTL check for CNAME failover as a fallback.

liam-net: dns records for vela private endpoint are on customer-managed DNS, but we do control an internal ELB CNAME for the dedicated pool. TTL is 60s on our internal record. We can update the CNAME to point to warm pool target-group.

maya-ops: creating canary route: 10% -> warm-1 now. Runbook step: /runbook incident/tenant-traffic-shift.

sachin-eng: note: warm pool instances use a slightly different model variant (quantized) — quality might differ. We'll set a payload-level fallback to the hosted-compatible variant if quality regressions detected.

kevin-sre: performing weight change now:
```
# aws elbv2 modify-target-group-attributes ... --target-group-arn arn:aws:...:vela-eu-west-warm-1
# traffic weights: pool-2=90, warm-1=10
```

maya-ops: 10% shifted. Monitoring error-rate and p99 latency on vela-tenant routes. Please ack when you see metrics.

anna-support: Vela CS updated customer: we have a mitigation in progress, shifting traffic to warm capacity. Asking if they want read-only maintenance page. They said no for now but want updates every 15m.

kevin-sre: metrics update: error-rate dropped from 12% -> 9% after 10% shift. p99 latency unchanged. Continuing to 30% in 3m if trend continues.

incident-bot: on-call handoff scheduled: current oncall tamara-oncall hands off to kevin-sre in 15 minutes per rota.

tamara-oncall: taking over now. I'm on the call with net to confirm CNAME fallback plan.

liam-net: CNAME ready to swap if shifting fails. Internal DNS update command: `aws route53 change-resource-record-sets --change-batch file://vela-failover.json --hosted-zone-id ZONE123`. The file sets CNAME from vela-eu-west-internal.example.com -> vela-eu-west-warm-1.elb.internal.example.com. TTL 60.

sachin-eng: watch model outputs for regressions. I'm running a quick eval harness against a golden prompt set for Vela feature-critical prompts.

kevin-sre: shifting to 30% now.

maya-ops: 30% shift done. Error-rate down to 4.5% overall. Canary traces show warm pool returning successful responses, but some increased tokenization latency for ~2% of requests.

anna-support: customer updated — they're seeing partial recovery. Asked for net-new retries to be minimized while we stabilize.

sachin-eng: eval harness: warm-model passes 92/100 golden prompts, two prompts show changed phrasing that may affect SLO for flavor-sensitive customers. Documenting and notifying product.

kevin-sre: plan: continue to 60% if errors keep falling. If regressions unacceptable, we will route only stateless requests to warm pool and let stateful flows failover by DNS (CNAME) as emergency.

tamara-oncall: 60% now. Monitoring. Handing off pages to kevin in 10m.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1845002468 — update recorded. Pager muted for noisy alerts.

maya-ops: 60% -> error-rate now 1.2%, p95 latency stable. Good signal.

liam-net: prepping DNS change for full cutover if needed. Note: we must coordinate with Vela's network team — their customer DNS TTL of 300s could delay external cutover. Internal ELB CNAME cutover will be near immediate.

anna-support: logged customer-facing incident note in CS system: Vela-12345, mitigation in progress, expected full recovery in <2h if current trend persists.

sachin-eng: can we increase warm pool autoscaling threshold for this tenant to ensure capacity? Current min replicas = 4, I'm raising min to 8 for warm-1 to reduce queuing.

kevin-sre: approved. Scaling group updates applied. New instances coming up; health checks green.

tamara-oncall: handing full on-call to kevin-sre now — I will be offline for 20m for a quick break. kevin, you're primary.

kevin-sre: acknowledged. continuing monitoring and will escalate to infra if errors bump.

maya-ops: 80% now. Error-rate ~0.6%. Warm pool handling fine.

anna-support: Vela CS confirms CS ticket updated; customer requests a postmortem and list of mitigation steps after incident.

sachin-eng: note for postmortem: root cause likely memory leak in a model adapter on pool-2 under a specific traffic pattern. Need heapprofiling on that variant.

kevin-sre: next steps: keep shifted traffic until we patch pool-2. Schedule rolling reboot + patch on pool-2 tonight during maintenance window, or rebuild nodes one-by-one. We'll coordinate with Vela for maintenance window.

liam-net: leaving DNS cutover as fallback. No external DNS changes yet.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1845002468 — resolved? Condition: error-rate <1% for 30m across tenant routes. Current: 0.6% for 25m. Awaiting confirmation.

maya-ops: will monitor 30m window.

kevin-sre: marking incident as mitigated for customer impact. Creating follow-up tasks:
- K1: deeper mem leak triage (sachin)
- K2: hardening warm pool autoscaling and pre-warm policies (ops)
- K3: customer postmortem + communication (anna)

anna-support: will coordinate postmortem and schedule customer sync.

tamara-oncall: back online and saw mitigation. Good job team.

incident-bot: INCIDENT 1845002468 — status set to MITIGATED by kevin-sre at 1845002789.

kevin-sre: closing thread. Will attach logs and runbook notes to the incident ticket.
